subject.title: Adopt Claude Code's multi-layer compaction architecture

question: Which Claude Code-inspired compaction layers should become canonical OpenClaw core behavior, and which should stay opt-in through providers, context engines, plugins, or runtime-specific Codex support?
rationale: The answer affects session-state durability, sensitive transcript/file exposure, config defaults, Codex-native compaction boundaries, and whether open PRs #58455 and #97580 should be repaired, split, or superseded.

options.title: Sponsor an incremental core architecture plan
options.body: Define the canonical compaction pipeline and land selected layers incrementally with explicit security, upgrade, and live-session proof.

options.title: Track only narrow repairs
options.body: Keep the existing core architecture and accept only small fixes such as partial-summary recovery or targeted pruning when each has independent proof.

options.title: Delegate experiments to extension seams
options.body: Use context-engine or compaction-provider/plugin APIs for advanced compaction strategies until a specific missing core seam is proven.

recommendation.title: Sponsor an incremental core architecture plan
recommendation.body: Define the canonical compaction pipeline and land selected layers incrementally with explicit security, upgrade, and live-session proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current checkout points to Peter Steinberger on the central compaction/context-pruning lines, and this decision cuts across core policy and product architecture rather than a single contributor PR.
